The rule with the MOST matching criteria wins (Valve dynamic dialogue, GDC 2012), ties are random, said lines rest `cool` days (default 4). Concepts: open, recall (kind), gossip (kind), accuse, remark, rumour, mutter, headline (verb). Criteria: see town_talk.gd header. Text: {npc} {player} {rival} {rival_short} {club} {days_left} {weekday} {place}. One rule per line - edit freely on the tablet.

t: "Oh - Asagiri-do's nephew. Morning, afternoon, whatever it is."
"You again. Good. The town needs new faces, it's bored of the old ones."
"Mm? Ah, the boy from Tokyo. Still here? Good for you."
"Watch your step. The pavement's slippery. It's always slippery."
"Hello, hello. Don't mind me, I'm only standing here."
"You've got that look. The one people get in their first year here."
"You're Haruka-chan's nephew, aren't you? You've got Genzo-san's ears."
"New in town? Don't answer, everybody knows. It's that kind of town."
"The Asagiri boy! Your grandfather used to buy his paper from me. Never paid on time. Always paid."
"Up early. School, is it? The hill is worse in the rain."
"Morning. The fish van's late, the bus is late, the sun is late. Normal day."
"Shouldn't you be in a classroom? I won't tell. The cats might."
"Skipping, are we? Your face says skipping."
"Lunch already? The yakisoba bread at the school store's gone by 12:31. Every day. I don't know who's buying it."
"School's out? Then go and be young somewhere. Not here. Here is for old people."
"After school is the best time in Suzunari. The light goes gold and nobody's in a hurry."
"Omagatoki. The hour you meet things. Don't answer if someone calls your name from behind."
"Look at that sky. Red like a lantern. My mother used to pull us indoors at this hour."
"Out late. The last bus leaves at 21:40 and it doesn't wait. Nor does the man who rides it."
"It's dark, boy. The steps aren't for tonight."
"No school today? Lucky. I haven't had a day off since 1998."
"Weekend! Go to the beach. Don't swim past the red buoy. Nobody swims past the red buoy."
"Rain again. Seventh day in a row. Or the seventieth. I've stopped counting."
"Here, stand under the awning. The rain in this town gets personal."
"Look at this storm! Somebody's very sad about something. That's what my grandmother would say."
"Get inside, boy, it's coming down sideways. The gutters can't keep up."
"Dry for once. Enjoy it. These things don't last here."
"Sun's out. Everybody's in a good mood. Don't ruin it."
"Welcome, welcome. Just looking? Looking's free. Breathing near the display is also free."
"Customer! Or not a customer. Either way, come in out of the weather."
"Eh? Speak up. My ears are seventy-eight years old."
"Young man. Sit with me a minute. Nobody sits with old people unless they want something."
"Asagiri-senpai, right? From 2-B? Everybody in first year knows who you are. Sorry."
"Oh! You're the one the hood boy follows. Um. Hi."
"Out of the way, boy, these crates won't carry themselves. ...Well. Morning."
"Smell that? That's the sea. You get used to it. Then you miss it."
"Asagiri. Shouldn't you be revising? I'm not your teacher. I'm a teacher. It's a professional reflex."
"Don't mind me. Four hours of commuting and a boss who calls on Sundays. Hello."
"Hey hey! You! Have you heard? No? Sit down, I'll start at the beginning."
"What."
"If you're selling something, I don't want it. If you're lost, the station's that way."
"Ah, hello. You look tired. Have a sweet. I always carry sweets."
"So. Where are you going? Who were you with? I'm only asking."
"Your little shadow isn't with you? The hooded one. He's usually three steps behind."
"The Nekomori boy was asking the cats where you were. Out loud."
"That first-year looked happy this morning. First time in nine years. Whatever you're doing, keep doing it."
"That first-year was crying at the bus stop again. Not my business. But it's raining, so it's everybody's business."
"Tanabata's coming. Have you written your wish yet? Write it small. The gods are nosy."
"{days_left} days to the festival. The whole street's arguing about lanterns."
"Late for school three times, I hear. The cats keep a record. So does Makabe-sensei."
"Shouldn't you be at school? Or have you stopped going? The cats say you've stopped going."
"I heard about the Inukai boy. Fell, they said. That family's had bad luck since the shrine went quiet."
"Have you seen {rival_short}? Nobody has. His mother walks up and down the street every evening."
"There's the Track Club runner. Hayate says you're getting faster. Hayate says a lot of things."
"Kendo club, aren't you? Your grandfather founded that club. Did you know? He was terrible at it."
"Go-Home Club? With the Nekomori boy as president? Well. Everybody needs a club."
"Newspaper Club. Tell Hayase-chan my cat is not 'the Shopping Street Menace'. She's a lady."
"You're on the council? Then tell them the gutter on this corner has been broken since the Showa era."
"Mio-chan's ghost club! Have you seen anything yet? Don't tell me. Do tell me."
"I can hear you practising from the street. Keep at it. Everybody starts bad."
"Cooking Club! Did you make the onigiri I saw on the roof? Too much salt. I could tell from here."
"Ah, the boy who works nights at the Mart. Does Yamane-san still do the top shelf herself?"
"I saw that. Your hand, their pocket. This isn't Tokyo, boy. Everybody knows everybody's pockets."
"Give it back. Whatever it was. The cats saw it too."
"Light fingers. Your grandfather would turn in his grave. He'd turn twice."
"That was kind of you, earlier. People notice. In this town people notice everything."
"You helped that one out. Good. Kindness gets around faster than gossip here. Almost."
"I saw what you did. Don't let it go to your head."
"You were shouting at someone earlier. I don't like shouting. The cats don't like shouting."
"Picking on people? You? I had you for the quiet sort."
"I saw you threaten that one. Next time pick on the gulls. They deserve it."
"Was that you singing earlier? Loudly? Near the bridge?"
"Quite a show you put on. My granddaughter filmed it. You're on her phone forever now."
"You were talking with {npc}'s neighbour this morning. Nice to see you making friends."
"Back again? You like talking. Most young people just look at their phones."
"Short of money, are you? Ask your aunt before you ask strangers. She'd want to know."
"Begging on the street. Haruka-chan would cry. Come by the shop if you're hungry."
"I saw you making a deal back there. Keep your business small, boy. Small business lasts here."
"Haggling? You haggle like your grandfather. Badly, with great confidence."
"You were doing something very strange by the lamp post earlier. I won't ask."
"What were you doing before? With the... the thing. Never mind. I don't want to know."
"Fighting in the street! In Suzunari! The last fight here was in 1987 and they still talk about it."
"Don't bring trouble here. We have enough with the weather."
"People say you took something that wasn't yours. Is it true? Don't tell me. I'll know anyway."
"Word on the street says you've got quick hands. Keep them in your pockets near me."
"They say you helped someone out. The whole street was talking. Nice for a change."
"Somebody said you bought old Matsumoto lunch. He hasn't stopped telling people."
"People say you've been throwing your weight around. Is that the Tokyo way?"
"The street says you scared someone. Scaring people here is the cats' job."
"They say you put on a show. My nephew says it was good. My nephew is tone-deaf."
"People say you talk to everyone. Good. Talk to me. Nobody talks to me."
"Somebody said you were asking strangers for money. Times are hard. Come see me first next time."
"They say you've been making deals. Little ones. Little ones become big ones. Careful."
"People are saying you're... odd. In a nice way. Mostly."
"The street says there was a fight. With you in it. Tell me that's a lie."
"Wait - it was you. The business at the shop. Everybody's heard. Don't come near my till."
"You've got a nerve, walking around after what happened. The whole street knows."
"Oh, it's you. The one everybody's talking about. The police were asking."
"You! The Suzunari Shimbun didn't print your name. They didn't have to."
"Tokyo boys always look like they're waiting for a train."
"You'll get used to the cats. They won't get used to you."
"Your aunt talks about you all the time. Don't tell her I said so."
"Kids from the city walk too fast. You'll slow down. Everybody does here."
"You look like someone who's trying not to be looked at. It isn't working."
"You're the one with the face from that noodle advert. 'Kitsune Udon, the taste of home!' I knew it!"
"Your aunt says you've got debts. At your age! Tell the shrine. The shrine likes a sad story."
"Your aunt said you had a bad time at your last school. Well. This is a different school."
"They say you were some kind of genius. You don't look like one. That's a compliment. Geniuses look tired."
"You walk like a man with nowhere to be. I like it. Suzunari likes it."
"Hayate's been telling the whole street you'll make the relay. No pressure."
"Gotoda-kun says you have courage. From Gotoda-kun that's a marriage proposal."
"I heard the Go-Home Club walks by the river. With the hooded boy. That's the most romantic club in Japan."
"Working nights and going to school? Your grandfather did the same. He was always asleep at the counter."
"The hooded first-year follows you like a shadow. My grandmother said shadows know who they belong to."
"That Nekomori boy waits for you outside the konbini. In the rain. Every day."
"Is it true you made that Nekomori boy cry? The whole street got soaked."
"Somebody's sad, with this weather. Is it you? You look like it might be you."
"Makabe-sensei says you actually listen in class. He was amazed. He told the fishmonger."
"Late again this week? You'll be late for your own wedding. My son was. Twice."
"You ask a lot of questions about the old stories. Careful. Old stories ask questions back."
"Chiyo-san at the shrine likes you. She hit you with her broom? That's how you know."
"They say it's rained every day since you came. Not saying it's you. Just saying."
"A cat with two tails was walking on the roofs last night. My husband saw it. My husband drinks, but still."
"The shrine bell rang by itself again. Nobody's rung that bell since 2010. Nobody living."
"Don't go to the station after the last train. People who do find the sign says a different name."
"The old tunnel by the harbour is sealed for a reason. Nobody remembers the reason. That's the reason."
"Kids say there's a girl in the third-floor toilet at the school. Knock three times and she answers. Don't."
"There's a fellow by the river with a dish on his head. If he bows, bow back. Deeper."
"The antique dealer is a tanuki. Everybody knows. Nobody minds. He gives a fair price."
"Count the steps up to the shrine. Nine hundred and ninety-nine. If you ever count a thousand, don't take the last one."
"The steps were built after the big wave in 1703. The cats were the ones who climbed first. That's why they own the hill."
"Never whistle by the river at night. The water comes to see who's calling."
"If you lose something by the river, leave a cucumber. You'll get it back. Wet."
"The last train plays Toryanse at the crossing. Going in is easy. Coming back is the frightening part. That's what the song says."
"A woman with a mask waits at the bus stop after dark. If she asks if she's pretty, say 'so-so'. Exactly 'so-so'."
"The fishermen saw lights on the water again. Six of them. Like little lanterns. Like little Jizo."
"On foggy mornings, if someone in a boat asks for a ladle, give them one with a hole in it."
"The shopping street association's lost the shrine bell rope. Again. Somebody's hiding it. Probably a cat."
"The Shirasagi family's buying up the closed shops. Every shutter on the street. Nobody knows what for."
"The school's Ura board posts a name every Monday. Whoever's named has a bad week. This week it was a second-year."
"There's a thirteenth step on the west staircase after six. Don't stand on it."
"The sea gave up six stone Jizo once, then took them back. It'll give them up again for the right person."
"My grandfather said the fish talk on the morning of a storm. He was a terrible liar and an excellent fisherman."
"In 2001 a boy ran away on the Tanabata train, and a girl cried on the steps all night. Ask your father, Asagiri. Ask him."
"Ten years ago a little boy went missing on the steps at Tanabata. Came back by morning and never said where he'd been."
"The library committee's recruiting. They promise snacks. They never have snacks."
"Somebody in second year runs the Ura board. Nobody knows who. Everybody suspects everybody."
"So it was Sato Yui running the Ura board all along. She's posting nicer things now. Suspiciously nice."
"Business is slow since 2010. The whole street went quiet when the shrine bell did. Coincidence, the bank says."
"The rain started the day you got off the train. The cats started following the Nekomori boy the same day. Make of it what you like."
"Golden Week festival on the shopping street! Hayase-chan's taking photos of everyone. Smile or hide."
"Something's going on with the Inukai boy's shoes. They keep going missing. Then turning up on the shrine steps."
"Midterms next week. The shrine sells out of exam charms. The cats sit on the books. It's tradition."
"Rainy season. As if we needed one."
"Hydrangeas by the jizo are blue this year. My mother said blue means someone's waiting."
"Sports festival! The relay's the only thing anyone cares about. And the bread-eating race."
"Somebody lit a lantern on the hill on the 13th night. Just one. At two in the morning. Old women know what that means."
"Everybody read Hayase-chan's article. Everybody's pretending they didn't."
"The heron company that bought the shops has an office in Tokyo with nobody in it. My son-in-law checked."
"The night parade comes down the steps before Tanabata. A hundred of them. Stay indoors and leave a light on."
"Tonight's the night. Tanabata. Everybody's going up the steps. Some of them will come down."
"They say the Inukai boy fell on the steps. Pushed, his father says. By what, he doesn't say."
"Spirited away, they're saying. Kamikakushi. Like the boy in 2016. That one came back."
"The cats have been sitting outside the Asagiri house at night. Facing the window. All of them."
That's Asagiri-do's nephew.
Tokyo boy.
Is it raining again?
The cats like him.
Did he grow?
Not my business.
Hands where I can see them.
That's the one.
That's the kind one.
Good boy, that one.
Don't look at him.
Trouble.
His shadow's here again.
The hood boy's watching.
Somebody's crying again.
This rain...
Late, isn't it?
Go home, boy.
SUZUNARI SHIMBUN: Shop on the high street reports a theft. 'We know who,' says the owner.
TOWN BOARD: Lost wallet reported. Cats questioned.
SUZUNARI SHIMBUN: Window broken on the shopping street. The association is 'disappointed'.
SUZUNARI SHIMBUN: Scuffle by the station. 'Not since 1987,' say residents.
TOWN BOARD: A kind stranger paid for someone's lunch. The whole street is talking.
SUZUNARI SHIMBUN: Resident 'spoken to firmly' near the river. Witnesses decline to say by whom.
TOWN BOARD: Someone was seen where they shouldn't be. Again.
TOWN BOARD: A complaint has been filed. The police are 'looking into it'. They are looking at the sea.
SUZUNARI SHIMBUN: Something happened. Nobody agrees on what.
